authoritativeSource.title: Music Braille Code 2015
facts: A meter signature is separated by blanks except when it immediately follows a key signature.
A change of meter is placed where it occurs and preferably with the following note.
The first note following a meter signature requires an octave mark.

inputBoundary.builderInvariant: time-signature changes must already land on derived measure boundaries

genericMidiSerialization.afterTickZero: emit at the start of the first measure using the new effective numerator/denominator when the effective meter differs from the previous measure
genericMidiSerialization.redundantIdenticalSourceEvent: do not emit an additional signature when effective meter is unchanged
genericMidiSerialization.keyAndMeterAtSameBoundary: key precedes meter with no intervening blank; Phase 14 still keeps key changes after tick 0 fail-closed

diagnostics.lossDisclosure: MIDI does not preserve whether print used common/cut-time symbols; numeric serialization remains the frozen profile.

realWorldAcceptance.expectedAfterImplementation: notation and bridge progress past the current meter-change blocker; 12/8 is emitted numerically and the next note has an octave mark

syntheticImplementationGates: 4/4 to 12/8 change at a measure boundary serializes numerically
first note after changed meter receives an octave mark
unchanged meter on the next measure is not redundantly emitted
4/4 is not converted to common time
2/2 is not converted to cut time
